notes: Upstream-clone bugfix task on matplotlib/matplotlib (v4.3 family, issue #31182): calling the histogram feature (Axes.hist / pyplot.hist) with duration data — numpy timedelta64 arrays or python datetime.timedelta objects — dies at the parent commit 496ae85214a7029d5c8eca320cb45f013b535dfe with an opaque numpy UFuncTypeError ('ufunc ''less'' did not contain a loop ...') or an unrelated '<' not supported TypeError instead of a clean explanatory error, because Axes.hist has no input check for duration dtypes and numpy binning then refuses to compare durations with floats. The agent gets the real tree detached at the parent (shallow, single commit; the fix commit c72236701f0371d37c8a3232133347d5b350bc59 is never fetched into the shipped clone) and must (1) write its own failing reproduction /app/repro.sh honouring MPL_TREE and demonstrate the symptom on both the repaired tree and a pristine pre-fix package copy baked at /opt/prefix (importable only via the meson-python editable hook skip var, which the instruction documents as tooling), (2) localise in a 4,551-file tree that the histogram function must reject duration inputs with TypeError whose message contains 'does not currently support timedelta inputs' (ambiguity 2: the reported failure is an opaque internal crash and the intended contract — fail fast with a friendly message, not make durations plottable — must be inferred), (3) implement the smallest fix (the real upstream change is a ~9-line input guard in Axes.hist; the verifier allows exactly one source file to differ from the parent blobs), (4) prove with the project's own regression test test_hist_timedelta_raises extracted from the fix commit at image build time via a throwaway clone (sha256-pinned, planted from /opt/golden at verify time), a 25-test green slice of the project's own test_axes.py hist suite, and five authored hidden cases reaching the same code path from inputs the upstream test does not use (other timedelta64 units/shapes incl. 2D and length-1, python timedelta with bins/range, multi-dataset hist where any dataset is a duration, a numeric/unaffected guard, and non-duration histogram TypeErrors keeping their own messages). Verifier additionally pin-snapshots site-packages at build time to close a sitecustomize monkeypatch hole, runs the agent repro both directions plus independent probes both directions (fixed tree must raise the clean TypeError; the pristine concept must still raise an opaque error and its copy identity is asserted via matplotlib.__file__), and runs the golden test both directions (pass on repaired tree, fail on the pre-fix concept). Measured fresh build at 1 CPU: ~55 s (apt 21s, pip 7s, shallow clone 6s, meson editable install incl. 8 compiled C extensions 19s); image 1.25 GB total / ~598 MB unique. Bug reproduces in-image with numpy 2.5.3: UFuncTypeError on timedelta64, TypeError '"<" not supported...' on datetime.timedelta; both fixed directions and the 25-test slice verified green with the real upstream fix applied. rubric total 12 -> medium. Reviewed: independent clone-based two-direction confirmation; bypass battery (hardcoded repro, env-keyed repro, out-of-scope-file fix, and a catch-and-repackage TypeError wrapper in _axes.py) — the first three already failed, the last originally passed and is now caught by hidden case h5; fix commit confirmed unreachable in the shipped image (cat-file fails, 1 commit).
